indicators.note: in places the fellow inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a fellow, some man, is referred to as him

explanation.surface: Someone assaults a man during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is a common crossword abbreviation for church; HIM goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime is to strike, as a clock or bell sounds the hour.

definitions.meaning: a clumsy, loutish rustic, a yokel working the clods of earth
a large, heavy shoe for trudging through fields

explanation.surface: A farm labourer is sacked from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the boot' looks like being fired; 'gets' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an oafish country labourer and the heavy footwear such people wore.

definitions.meaning: the charge paid on borrowed money, a percentage over the loan
a stake or involvement in something, or curiosity about it

explanation.surface: Paying off a loan leaves a person worried.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the money paid for a loan and a stake or attentiveness one has in a matter.

parts.note: the crosses are marks voters put on ballot papers, which decide who wins a poll

explanation.surface: A puzzle about crosses settling a result, perhaps in noughts and crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote is decided by the X marks voters make on their ballot papers.

definitions.meaning: a harsh, unfavourable remark or attack
a piece of brick thrown as a weapon

explanation.surface: Someone is criticising a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a fragment of brick hurled at someone, and figuratively a cutting remark of disapproval.

definitions.meaning: endured, the past tense of bear
a surge of water running up a river estuary as the tide comes in

explanation.surface: Someone was hit by a tsunami.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn bore is a famous tidal surge in the UK's River Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of bear means endured; it is also a tidal surge moving upriver.

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
consumes means the medic swallows the next word inside it

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic
uncooked food is raw

explanation.surface: A doctor who has stopped working eats raw chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns the whole container (DRAWOC) round, not just the medic; 'chicken' looks like food beside 'uncooked' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken is slang for someone timid who lacks courage.

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a second team is a B side, the reserve eleven in cricket or football

explanation.surface: A reserve team manages to scrape through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word; 'by' looks like part of 'gets by' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: By means next to, as in a house by the sea.

definitions.meaning: a single droplet of liquid from the eye
a rip or split in fabric

explanation.surface: A fall in how much is charged for housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, it is both a droplet shed when crying and a rip in cloth.

clue.text: About to get the song broadcast

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A singer is about to have the song played on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being transmitted live is going out to listeners, so it is being broadcast.

clue.text: Maybe Eli's pear was plucked from it

definitions.text: Maybe Eli's pear was plucked from it

indicators.note: plucked suggests pulling apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eli's pear may have been picked from a fruit-tree framework.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a pear grown flat against a trellis may be picked from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis or framework against which fruit trees such as pears are trained flat.

clue.text: Rushed to get top spaniel groomed

indicators.note: top means the first letter of spaniel

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb

explanation.surface: A dog owner hurried to get the best spaniel brushed for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top spaniel' reads as a champion dog, but 'top' just picks S.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurried means moved hastily with short quick steps.

clue.text: A car not easy to beat

parts.note: something not easy is hard
to top something is to beat or exceed it

explanation.surface: An unbeatable motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle with a rigid fixed roof, as opposed to a convertible.

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Workers are upset by a plan to make staff redundant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redundancy' suggests job losses; here it means needless repetition of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical term for using more words than necessary, as in 'free gift'.

clue.text: Many a strip features Pauline Fowler, for example

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, many
to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A comic strip often shows a soap-opera character.
explanation.walkthrough: Pauline Fowler was a character in the British TV soap EastEnders who worked at the launderette.
explanation.definitionFit: The character's job was washing clothes, the work of a woman who launders.

clue.text: How to climb the ladder slowly but surely

definitions.meaning: ascending a ladder rung by rung
gradually, one stage at a time

explanation.surface: Advice on careful career progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes going up a ladder one rung at a time and progressing gradually.

clue.text: Apply skills on becoming a GP

definitions.meaning: to use what one has learned in reality
joining a doctors' practice as a family doctor, a general practitioner

explanation.surface: A medical student uses what they've learned on qualifying as a family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP (general practitioner) is a British family doctor working in a practice.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry out theory in reality; humorously, also to place someone in a medical surgery.

definitions.meaning: to pay off what one owes, clearing the account
a command to leave, go

explanation.surface: Someone told to pay up, then told to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to pay off fully and, as an order, to depart.

clue.text: Really wanted to dine out with husband and daughter

indicators.note: out signals the word dine is rearranged

parts.note: a husband is a man, as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A family dinner out with husband and daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sought after by many people is popular and much requested.

clue.text: Sappers need transport for news items

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers
portage is the carrying of boats or goods overland

explanation.surface: Army engineers require vehicles for delivering news.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; RE (Royal Engineers) is the British corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news events, journalism.

definitions.meaning: police slang for taking someone into custody
a roadside stop where lorry drivers eat

explanation.surface: Police arrest someone at a roadside café.
explanation.walkthrough: A transport café is a cheap British roadside diner for lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to detain a suspect and is also a British term for a roadside lay-by café.

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: The keenest set of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group of painters' gives a ring of Royal Academicians, so the painters come first in the answer though named last.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, means eager to the utmost degree.

clue.text: Impersonator right to appear in dull fabrics

indicators.note: the impersonator and right appear inside the word for dull

parts.note: dry speech is dull or boring
to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: A mimic dressed in drab clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impersonator right' reads as one phrase, but the mimic and the abbreviation are two pieces that 'to appear in' places together inside the dull word.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapery is cloth or textiles, especially hanging folds of material.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, many
vintage means old
rums are spirits

explanation.surface: Drinking lots of old spirits makes someone gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums means being in low spirits or a slump.

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Many people here are grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour describes a gloomy, stern, unfriendly manner.

clue.text: But don't spend all your money

definitions.meaning: except, as in all ... one
put money aside rather than spending it

explanation.surface: Advice against spending one's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means except and also to keep money rather than spend it.

clue.text: Proud to go around in sheer clothing

indicators.note: clothing means wrapping the outer word around another

parts.note: arrant means utter or sheer

indicators.note: around means the word go is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Feeling superior about wearing see-through clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' signals a container, with 'around' turning the go to OG; 'sheer clothing' looks like see-through garments, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant means haughty and conceited.

indicators.note: direly means dreadfully, so the letters are badly mixed

explanation.surface: An Englishman is enraged by someone abandoning their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or faith, as an apostate does.

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, a fed in American slang
up means cheerful or elated

explanation.surface: Is the FBI agent happy? Not at all!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anything but!' means the opposite of elated, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thoroughly disgruntled is the reverse of being happy.
